boulders-text:
Introduction to Prospecting with IOG
Because of some issues with vanilla prospecting code, I had to disable a function that causes the vanilla Density Search Mode to almost fail entirely (the mode where you're looking at %% numbers). Do not use this mode unless you have Betterer Prospecting installed.

Prospecting with Vanilla IOG
Vanilla InterestingOreGen has a built in way to prospect for ores without needing the prospecting pickaxe density search mode.

In the world you'll find boulders lying around of a host rock type. These boulders are indicators of a vein deposit somewhere in the vicinity. The ore will be of the same host rock type as the boulders. If you're not using a prospecting pickaxe density search mode you can locate the rough region of an ore vein just by looking for boulders. The spread, and quantity of boulders can roughly tell you the depth and size of the vein.

Once you've found some boulders, you can use the Node Search Mode on a prospecting pickaxe to find tracer veins nearby clusters of boulders. Tracer veins are small shoots of ore that spread off of the main ore body and reach the surface stone layer (Under dirt). Once you locate a tracer vein on the surface you can mine down and follow it to the main ore body. Keep in mind Tracer Veins are not lines, and are designed to be confusing and hard to follow!

Tracer Veins and Boulders
Tracer veins and boulders are actually created through the same mechanism. The mechanism is, at a small % chance for every ore block placed, the snake will climb it's way to the surface stone layer. This snake when it reaches the stone layer has a 30% chance of becoming a boulder, and a 70% chance of becoming a tracer vein. If it becomes a boulder it will NOT place any ore, whatsoever. Boulders DO NOT (generally) have tracer veins under them. (This mod is RNG so sometimes you *may* find tracers under, around, or even in boulders, but the chance is very small).

Traver veins are designed to be tricky and sneaky. Logic wise, they will always go UP one block, and POSSIBLY go over 1 block in any 8 orthogonal or diagonal directions. They also have a bias direction they will go more often than other directions, but can double back on themselves and even corcscrew or do other funky things. One thing to keep in mind though, sometimes you'll come to a vein end that looks like it may have jumped 2 blocks in either up or side direction. Tracer veins have an approximately 30% chance *not* to place ore, so sometimes it will have moved 1 up and over, but not placed an ore block to follow! When in doubt dig a pyramid down below your last found ore block in a 1x1 step slope.

Ross's Recommended Prospecting Guide
Step 1: Locate boulders
Step 2: Remove the soil layers on the surface, or if you don't want to remove loads of dirt, dig a small tunnel just under the surface in the rock to locate a tracer vein.
Step 3: Follow tracer vein down to main ore body
Step 4: Profit.?

Betterer Prospecting
Betterer Prospecting directly fixes the issue with vanilla prospecting, and makes it an absolute method of prospecting. If you don't want to use IOG's Tracer Veins and Boulders I HIGHLY recommend using Betterer Prospecting by KnewOne
caveins-text:
IOG Cave-Ins and Stability Logic!
Interesting Ore Gen comes built in with a new and improved cave-in system. It's more consistent and better performing than the vanilla cave-in system. You can disable or enable this with the world setting or with the command /worldconfig caveIns [on/off], however you either use no cave-in logic, or IOG's cave-in logic. I have disabled vanilla cave-in for a few technical reasons. (There is no way to use Vanilla Cave-in Logic with IOG currently)

Cave-in Logic for IOG should be mostly simple to understand for a player. That is, any block with 100% instability and has air under it has a (decently high) chance to collapse. It's not as simple as search around the player and find X block though!

Keeping in mind that blocks that *can* initiate a collapse HAVE to be exposed to air on their BOTTOM face, means you can technically prevent a collapse by simply plastering your mine ceiling with blocks of any kind that can float. (Wood, stone, etc.) There are other ways to mine though! Such as Room and Pillar, where you only remove most of the ore, but leave natural support beams of material supporting the ceiling. Or supporting it with Support Beams (I highly recommend the Post and Beams mod! they're better in a TON of ways), or open pit if you like suffering! There's many ways to mine your ore, figure out what you feel up to and best application for your situation.

Technical Details
The average player should actually read this too!
The collapse logic for IOG is kind of complicated under the hood, but to simplify it as much as I can: Every time a player breaks a block, from the block broken an Orthogonal (touching faces only) step-search begins from the block broken. This travels up to 20 steps/blocks and has a few rules to keep in mind. The Step-search checks each block it's touching on it's face and will about 70% of the time go towards the highest instability block. It also will bias travelling upward very slightly. That means in effect it will generally follow the highest instability block and go until either it runds out of steps, or finds a block with 100% instability. When the Step-Search finds 100% unstable blocks, it will travel directly downwards checking each block. It will check if that block's bottom is an air block. If it's air, it will initiate a collapse. Otherwise, it will do nothing.

When a collapse is initiated, it creates a virtual ellipsoid centered on the collapse, and then will offset it up to 5 blocks upwards. The radius of this ellipsoid begins at a maximum of 8 and can go up to 12 in some directions due to some deformation logic. Generally it can also be as small as 4 blocks in diameter. Every block within the ellipsoid that has instability logic will instantly be converted to gravel and will fall. If it's ore it will remain ore. This is to allow cleaning up, as if it were cracked stone or something it might cause issues cleaning up collapses.
veins-text:
This is a rough overview of the progression plans of the mod

The rough progression of the mod is meant to be centered around long range exploration, establishment of large infrastructure to minesites and 'Find once Cry once' policy. Certain ores are only obtainable from the (brand new as of writing this) True Fault veins (Hydrothermal Districts). You can only find Chromite, Ilmenite, Pentlandite, Sulfur, and Cinnabar in these structures. (Also honorable mention is Saltpeter Ore blocks).

There are 4 types of hydrothermal districts, here is their info:

Cold Hydrothermal District
Host Material: Travertine
Available Ores: Sulfur, Cinnabar, Malachite, Saltpeter, Halite, Borax, Alum, and Sylvite

Magmatic-Felsic Shallow
Host Material: Granitic Quartz (Quartz in Granite)
Available Ores: Gold, Silver, Galena, Sphalerite, Bismuthinite, Cinnabar, Sulfur, and Alum

Magmatic-Granitic Deep
Host Material: Granite
Available Ores:Cassiterite, Bismuthinite, Gold (in quartz), Sphalerite, and Galena

Magmatic-Mafic Shallow
Host Material: Basalt
Available Ores: Native Copper, Magnetite, Ilmenite, Pentlandite, Sulfur, Limonite, Chromite


Older IOG Veintypes
Currently there are only 3 major vein types in the mod:
Chimney is a series of vertical or nearly vertical chutes of ore that form very deep under the ground, and reach up like some horrible rock fingers.
Hydrotube are large complexes of often horizontal thin tubes that branch and spread out. Often over extremely large areas like is the case in Malachite.
Seam deposits are large warped disks underground reserved primarily for "sedimentary" type ores, or ores that form in large sheets in real life such as Iron and Coals. There is also a vertical variant of this used in some ore types such as Native Copper and Bismuth, but I've turned these way down with the new addition of the hydrothermal districts. I will not maintain a complete list of what ores spawn in what veins, as that changes from update to update and rapidly becomes outdated information.
